Emphasis ticks, rules and counts take {token} ({resolved}); the colour stays a highlight only, never a field or a fill.

values.change: Stale rows keep the current treatment: conflict-red border and red age text, as loud as blocked rows.

Stale rows drop to the muted offline treatment (ground --panel-2, text --muted) with the age printed and a gold tick in --accent; conflict red becomes blocked-only, and a row both stale and blocked renders as blocked with its age still printed.
Cards sit flat on the ground with a fine divider in --line; no border box, no shadow.
Cards carry a 1px border in --line over --panel; no shadow, no glow.
Cards lead with their count as a large numeral in the package type scale; the numeral is text, never an image.

evidence.note: The dimension list mirrors the tweak panel the second Claude Design tutorial (TcFeSjwTo7g, 14:55-17:39) had the generator invent: palette/theme, accent hue, section rhythm, card style. Two of the tutorial's dimensions are deliberately absent: font and headline case/scale are not declared because their bounds are not package material yet — the package's font stacks are unruled placeholders, so a font dimension would slide between invented values. A dimension whose bounds are not in the package is inexpressible here, by design.

The stale-treatment dimension's default ('shout') is the boards' current behaviour, measured by the Slice 3 verify gate: stale rows render with a conflict-red border and red age text, as loud as blocked rows (proof findings: 0 fail, 2 warn, 35 info; the headline warn). 'quiet' restates the boards-stale-quiet candidate plan as an explorable setting.

Every token and theme named in the bounds exists in this package's design.json: themes base/light, tokens --accent (#d4af37) and --brand (#73fd7c), and the spacing ladder --space-4 (1rem) / --cluster-gap (1.25rem) / --space-6 (1.5rem). The validator re-resolves them on every run; if the package changes under the manifest, validation goes red rather than letting the space drift off-brand.

INVENTED — Dave's review surface: the choice of these five dimensions for the boards, the card-style options and their default ('flat'), and the accent-role alternative (brand green for emphasis) are candidates authored for this slice. The locks they explore inside are Dave's (palette relationships, gold highlight-only, restraint); the dimensions themselves are not settled until he rules.

summary: The bounded exploration space for the Fleet Boards surface: five dimensions Dave may flip while reviewing the boards, every one bound to the nougenai-brand package's own tokens, themes, or enumerated treatments. Exploring changes nothing; settling produces a candidate variant plan that only Dave's lock can apply.
